extracted.intended_audience: prospective PCMI applicants: mathematics researchers, graduate students, undergraduates, and undergraduate faculty
extracted.subtask_description: Informational page describing the IAS/Park City Mathematics Institute three-week residential summer session (PCMI) for 2026, summarizing the Research Program, Graduate Summer School, Undergraduate Summer School (including XML), Undergraduate Faculty Program, application availability, dates, organizers, and funding acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The IAS/Park City Mathematics Institute (PCMI) is an intensive three-week residential conference; for 2026 it will be held June 28–July 18, 2026 in Park City, Utah.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session is residential and intensive, bringing multiple parallel programs together during the three-week period.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCMI 2026 Research Topic
rubrics_metrics.description: PCMI 2026 Research Topic: Knotted Surfaces in Four-Manifolds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized by R. İnanç Baykur, Kyle Hayden, András Stipsicz, Gordana Matic, Masaki Taniguchi, and Ian Zemke. Details on the Research Program are available via the provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate Summer School
rubrics_metrics.description: Course descriptions and additional information on the Graduate Summer School program can be found via the linked Graduate Summer School page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Graduate Summer School consists of short courses appropriate for graduate students; further specifics are provided on the linked page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate Summer School and Experimental Math Lab (XML)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Undergraduate Summer School will consist of a three-week program led by Mark Hughes (Brigham Young University) and an interactive Experimental Math Lab (XML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information about the Undergraduate Summer School and the XML is available via the provided link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate Faculty Program (UFP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Undergraduate Faculty Program will be a three-week program led by Jeffrey Meier (Western Washington University).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details for the 2026 UFP are available through the linked UFP page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application availability and encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for the 2026 PCMI Summer Session are available now; PCMI encourages applications from all those with interest in the program, both from the US and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's goal is to provide a welcoming community for all participants; contact pcmi@ias.edu with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel programs / participant-targeted activities
rubrics_metrics.description: PCMI includes several parallel sets of activities aimed at different groups across the mathematics community: program for mathematics researchers, short courses for graduate students, lecture series for undergraduate students, and an undergraduate faculty program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the annual Summer Session, all programs meet simultaneously, pursuing individual courses of study and participating in cross-program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-program interaction principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-program activities are based on the principle that each group has something important to teach and to learn from the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interaction is intended to enrich participants, increase appreciation of the mathematical community, and raise understanding of issues confronting mathematics and mathematics education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Major funding from Simons Foundation and National Science Foundation; with generous support from the Clay Mathematics Institute Senior Scholar Program.
